name: Labi-labi

narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: A local cultural historian or traditional dancer from Pahang.
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated in the 1950s in Kampung Sarang Tiong, Endau, Kuala Rompin, Pahang.
It emerged from local observations of the soft-shell turtle and evolved through three distinct regional versions in Pahang, including those in Kampung Pulau Rumput and Kampung Jambu.
on_screen: Map: Malaysia · Southeast Asia

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance was created as a form of humorous entertainment for the community.
It serves to celebrate local stories, such as the successful catch of a labi-labi, and to foster laughter and social bonding.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance involves the imitation of the labi-labi's movements.
Dancers use exaggerated facial expressions and humorous physical actions to entertain the audience.
In some versions, the movement is influenced by martial arts, while in others, it is a direct mimicry of the turtle's behavior.
Watch for Labi-labi mimicry.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Ms. Siti (whose craving inspired the dance), her husband, Encik Iderus bin Ginuh (who brought the dance to Kampung Pulau Rumput), and Pak Ngah Hitam (who developed the version in Kampung Jambu).
The dance exists in three primary versions based on location: Kampung Sarang Tiong, Kampung Pulau Rumput, and Kampung Jambu, each with slightly different origins and influences.
The dance is a traditional Malay folk dance.

music_brief.purpose: original soundtrack faithful to the tradition, with documented commercial reuse rights and no recurring royalties
music_brief.rights_rule: A composition brief does not clear an output. Record the provider/model/version, terms and date, input rights, output licence, restrictions and review before release.
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Labi-labi (Malaysia). Mood: humorous, entertaining, funny. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.

wardrobe.policy: neutral dress: the sources do not describe the costume yet
care: every element traceable to the costume notes or a licensed image; nothing added for effect
no caricature, no exaggeration, no mixing of regions or eras
a culture bearer reviews the wardrobe before production; the review is recorded in the pack
credits name the tradition and the sources of the reconstruction

visual_brief.setting_notes: The dance was created as a form of humorous entertainment for the community. It serves to celebrate local stories, such as the successful catch of a labi-labi, and to foster laughter and social bonding.
